levels.name: NYC Bar
levels.blocker: BODY model model2 -- 3 world LightMap records get an iLightActors run UED22 leaves at -1 (Lights 484 vs 478, LightBits 6003 vs 5891); leaf permeating region is clean. Root-caused 2026-09-12: Light5 (the first N it enters the trunk) sits beside a closed door (DeusExMover9, a Mover) standing exactly in the world-BSP opening between it and 3 stair treads. Confirmed by direct probe that native's world-level GetVisibleSurfs itself (not the per-lumel raytrace) wrongly lists the 3 treads as visible -- native's world gather never sees mover geometry, so it lights straight through the closed door. Mirror-image evidence: model model_deusexmover9 ALSO fails N=153, missing Light5 on the door's own face where UED22 has it. This is visible_surfs.rs's documented 'moving-brush filter (step 3)' gap, flagged as 'assumed to never fire' -- confirmed here to fire. Not fixed: the real fix unifies the world and mover light bakes into one scene (UED22's FMovingBrushTracker mirrors each mover poly into a transient world surf during the bake, per unbuilt.light_apply_movers's own docstring) -- a structural change, not a local patch.

levels.name: UNATCO HQ
levels.blocker: BODY model model2 -- leaf 12 gets a permeating-light run (Light157) UED22 leaves empty. Confirmed (2026-09-12) as the SAME shared-portal-vertex sub-ULP tie as Island N=332: live gdb capture of the editor's real ActorVisibility flood independently pinpointed the identical decisive crossing (13->12) that native's own trace found -- both sides compute a beam-clip vertex that should equal a shared portal vertex; native ties exactly (0 ULP, collapses the edge, lets the beam through); the editor's live capture differs by ~1 ULP (real nonzero edge, blocks it). Not a fix -- a second independent reproducer. Also corrects Island N=332's 'x87 vs SSE' hypothesis: this build's Engine.dll/Editor.dll are SSE2-only (no x87 control-word use), so x87 extended precision is unlikely to be the cause.

levels.name: OceanLab
levels.blocker: BODY model model2 -- world Model2.points holds a 2-ULP-off value pair native/UED22 disagree on (same array length, 3776=3776, so a value divergence not a reordering). Real effort spent, root cause NOT found: ruled out the brush483/brush1423 transform, a direct FLinePlaneIntersection crossing against the obvious x=-256 plane, and every split_with_plane crossing near that point (~5500 live-instrumented hits, none matched). Likely a different point-pooling/insertion-order gap from the already-fixed MergeNearPoints/pBase class -- needs the same live-editor-probe effort (winedbg) that produced today's other breakthroughs. No exclusion proposed.

levels.name: WanChai Market
levels.blocker: N=58: leaf 51 gets an extra permeating-light entry -- same shape as N=45 but a DIFFERENT cause: the crossing itself is fine, what differs is the beam polygon carried into the leaf. N=45's real bug is FIXED (BREAKTHROUGH): FPoly::SplitWithPlaneFast's crossing vertex comes from FLinePlaneIntersection's exact formula (Sc = (W - dot(P1,N)) / dot(D,N); out = Sc*D + P1), not native's mathematically-equivalent alpha = dp/(dp-ds) -- same real number, different f32 rounding, which on WanChai collapsed a downstream clip edge to zero length and let a beam through a boundary it should have stopped at. This is the SAME root cause already fixed for Island/OceanLab/UNATCO's shared leaf-permeating class -- WanChai N=45 was its cheapest reproducer.

levels.name: UNATCO Island
levels.blocker: BODY model model2 -- leaf 273 gets a permeating-light run (Light124) UED22 leaves empty. Root-caused: a genuine vertex coincidence -- a portal vertex shared exactly with an adjacent portal, where one FLinePlaneIntersection crossing lands a hair below the shared point in native and a hair above it in a live editor capture (same formula, same inputs, opposite sign of a sub-ULP residual). UNATCO N=226 (2026-09-12) independently reproduced the identical mechanism at a different crossing via live gdb capture, confirming this isn't Island-specific. The earlier 'x87 vs SSE double-rounding' hypothesis is now considered unlikely: a pre-existing spike shows this build's Engine.dll/Editor.dll are SSE2-only with zero x87 control-word use. Not fixed; needs single-stepping the editor's real FLinePlaneIntersection under gdb at the exact crossing to find the register-level cause.
